title: USMARC 212 sorghum: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: USMARC 212 sorghum: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: USMARC 212 sorghum is a sorghum variety. About 118 days to harvest, 4.4 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: USMARC 212 is a registered sorghum variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 1994 as NSIC 1994 Sg 02. USM bred it. It takes about 118 days from planting to harvest, with 4.4 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [sorghum variety finder](/crop-varieties/sorghum), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for corn and grains](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 118 days from planting to harvest.
**Yield:** 4.4 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** the areas in its trials, in the dry season.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

USMARC 212 sorghum takes about 118 days from planting to harvest. That is 14.8 days longer than the average of the 3 sorghum varieties with a day count, 103.2 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 4.4 t/ha trails the average of its group, 5.07. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose).

The pests and diseases that hit sorghum fields most often: [Rice birds (maya)](/pests/rice-birds), [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [Corn planthopper](/pests/corn-planthopper). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant USMARC 212 sorghum
It is recommended for the dry season. Sorghum stands drought better than corn, so it fits the dry season and dry uplands. Pick by use: grain for food and feed, or sweet sorghum for juice and syrup.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 118 days from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 4.4 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of USMARC 212?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
